system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Project Kestrel — Buyer review

The Seller’s description of its terms as “market”, “agreed” and “FINAL” is not evidence that Wattlebridge accepted them. The recommendations below are buyer opening positions, subject to the complete SPA, due diligence and commercial instructions.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty claims capped at 20% of price: **AUD 4.8m**. | A higher cap, ideally **100% of price**, with separate treatment for fundamental claims and indemnities. | **Reject; counter at 100%.** A 20% cap may leave the Buyer carrying substantial undisclosed business risk. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; only losses above an aggregate **AUD 250,000** basket are recoverable. | A lower de minimis and a **tipping basket**, under which the full amount is recoverable once the threshold is exceeded; exclude fundamental claims and specific indemnities. | **Counter with AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket.** The proposed deductible basket transfers the first AUD 250,000 of qualifying losses to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months** after Completion; limitations apply to all claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with longer, separately stated periods for tax, fundamental warranties and identified risks; a valid notice should preserve the claim for a reasonable period to pursue it. | **Counter at 24 months and separate claim categories.** Eighteen months may not cover two full audit cycles or allow latent issues to emerge. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties have the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate fundamental warranties, including ownership, authority and unencumbered title; a cap of at least **100% of price**, no general thresholds, and a longer survival period. | **Reject the general regime for fundamental warranties.** The Buyer must have meaningful recourse if it does not receive the shares it is buying. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Caps, limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to **all claims of any nature**; no express fraud exception is stated. | An express carve-out for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment from caps, thresholds, time limits, disclosure, knowledge, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the extent legally permissible. | **Require an overriding fraud carve-out.** The current blanket language could be used to argue that contractual restrictions limit fraud remedies. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | The entire indexed data room, accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records are generally disclosed. | Only matters **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail** to identify their nature and scope against relevant warranties; remove blanket data-room and public-record disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure; require specific, fairly disclosed matters.** Mere presence in a large data room should not automatically extinguish warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by the Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete the qualifier; if unavoidable, limit it to **actual knowledge** of named individuals, without imputed or constructive knowledge, and preserve claims under specific indemnities and for fraud. | **Reject discoverability and adviser imputation.** The clause would shift diligence risk to the Buyer even where no one identified the issue. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; consent condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DD-002 records approximately **AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue**, and consent conditions; final consent and evidence of satisfaction are absent. | A condition precedent requiring valid, unconditional consent—or consent on terms acceptable to the Buyer—and satisfaction or waiver of associated conditions before Completion; stronger Seller obligations to obtain it. | **Do not complete without verified consent and satisfied conditions.** A written consent alone may not preserve a customer representing approximately 30% of revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; release is to follow Completion. No final discharge is included. | Completion repayment from Seller proceeds under a lender payout letter, with simultaneous release/discharge arrangements and evidence of authority; reflect debt in the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics. | **Require repayment and effective release at Completion, not an unsecured post-Completion promise.** Otherwise the Buyer risks acquiring debt and encumbered assets. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses are omitted from funds flow; tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unresolved. | Confirm conditions and on-costs; make the Seller economically responsible for the bonuses and associated costs through an explicit price/debt adjustment or funded Completion payment, without double counting. | **Itemise and allocate the full liability before signing.** Completion-triggered obligations could otherwise remain in the Company at the Buyer’s expense. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment. DD-010 shows **AUD 180,000 open**, but does not independently prove non-payment; payment receipt and confirmatory assignment are absent. | Verify payment and obtain a confirmatory assignment of relevant IP; broaden the indemnity to cover losses, third-party claims, remediation and replacement arising from the SOW3 payment or transfer issue. | **Require evidence and broader specific protection.** Paying the fee alone may not resolve ownership or consequential claims. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller calls DD-006 preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope, notification and loss remain unconfirmed. | Complete investigation and assess notification/remediation obligations; require disclosure updates, cooperation and a specific indemnity for resulting losses, including reasonable response costs, subject to appropriate legal limits. | **Keep open and seek a tailored indemnity.** The unknown facts do not establish a breach, but the potential exposure cannot yet be assessed. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling **AUD 330,000** are characterised as ordinary-course costs; DD-008 and DD-011 do not establish whether they are unavoidable, accrued or terminable. | Reconcile each renewal’s timing, commitment, termination rights and accrual; allocate any pre-Completion liability or non-ordinary-course commitment through the agreed price mechanics or specific protection, without double counting. | **Investigate before accepting the Seller’s characterisation.** The record does not establish that all three are ordinary-course future costs. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General limitations and all-claims language may apply across warranties, indemnities and other claims. | An express hierarchy and separate regimes for general and fundamental warranties, tax covenant, specific indemnities, price adjustments and other claims; identify the cap, threshold and period for each. | **Rewrite the interaction provisions.** A specific protection may be materially weakened if general limitations silently apply. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 records Harbourglass as holder of **100% of issued shares**; Seller relies on the register. | Verify the register and supporting corporate records, issued capital, transfers, options and encumbrances; obtain clean-title warranties and Completion deliverables transferring all shares. | **Verify independently and retain robust title protection.** The register is relevant evidence, not conclusive proof that all shares can be transferred free of competing rights. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller treats tax and IP warranties as settled under the general regime. | A separate **pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity**, appropriately longer claims period and tax warranties; substantive IP ownership, assignment, licensing and infringement warranties, plus the Ironquay protection. Set separate liability treatment expressly. | **Reopen both workstreams.** General warranties alone may not adequately address historic tax liabilities or ownership of the Company’s core technology. |

**Other diligence point:** DD-007 identifies an office-lease **notification**, not a stated consent requirement; DD-009 identifies an assignment restriction, not a stated change-of-control consent. Check the underlying terms and comply where required, but do not assume either consent is needed solely from this disclosure.
=== END ADVICE ===
